initial.oxygen: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Create a new photographic educational asset for a sophisticated astronaut health application. The attached photograph is a PHYSICAL HARDWARE REFERENCE, not a scene to reproduce. Keep the recognizable construction of the real fingertip oximeter: yellow molded outer case, black inner clip, actual hinge, a small power button, dark glass display marked SpO2 and PR bpm. Do not invent a smooth white sci-fi device. Show it correctly fitted over a bare index fingertip, nail pointing toward the upper jaw, natural hand anatomy. One single hand and forearm extends from the lower right, relaxed, palm angled down. The hand belongs to an adult crew member wearing a worn charcoal-gray cotton flight-shirt sleeve, not a spacesuit glove. Close, candid macro documentary photograph inside a dim spacecraft: believable warm reflected cabin light on the yellow plastic, very subtle cool blue fill on the skin. Visible fine hairs, pores, shallow creases, cuticles, slight dry skin, cloth fibers, real tiny scuffs on the housing. Understated, grounded photographic realism, not a luxury product render. Device fills about a quarter of a wide 3:2 image, hand fills center and lower right; every finger visible has correct anatomy, no extra or fused fingers. Keep all important hardware entirely inside the frame with margin. Display powered but numbers not readable, never communicate a specific patient result. Isolated photographic cutout with genuinely transparent background, including transparent negative space around the hand; no rectangle, no room, no table, no star field, no text captions, no arrows, no border, no floor shadow, no fake holograms. No new branding or certification marks. The lighting and practical cotton sleeve evoke a lived-in spacecraft. It must look touched and used, not pristine or airbrushed.
initial.pressure: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Create a new photographic educational asset for an astronaut health application. Do not invent a featureless white device. Do not reproduce the person or room. Show a candid close-up of an adult crew member's bare upper arm and relaxed forearm, with a properly sized dark woven cuff fitted directly to bare skin above the elbow bend. A gray cotton short sleeve is rolled clear of the cuff. The cuff is snug, no loose flap, no sleeve trapped underneath. A real flexible air tube leaves the cuff and connects visibly to the monitor, secured beside the forearm by a simple fabric equipment strap; it must not float impossibly. Crop above the shoulder so there is no face. Forearm relaxed, hand naturally open, correct human anatomy. Show a complete plausible device, cuff and tube within the image. Wide 3:2 composition: arm diagonal across center, monitor lower right, ample transparent margin around the whole assembly. Documentary close-up in a dim, lived-in spacecraft, soft practical cabin lighting, restrained cool blue reflection and warm skin highlights, subtle skin pores, natural body hair, cuff weave, slightly worn cotton fibers, small real scuffs and joins in plastic. This should look like a real captured onboard training photograph, not a CGI product render or sterile advertisement. LCD is inactive or unreadable; no patient numbers. Genuinely transparent background, no environment rectangle, no table, no stars, no interface, no arrows, no text captions, no borders, no invented holograms or certification. Keep the device grounded and recognizable, with believable imperfect materials.

prompts.lancingPlacement: A single square, close photographic medical-training illustration of a capped spring-loaded finger-prick lancing pen correctly used on the FLESHY SIDE of a fingertip. Use the attached manufacturer's diagram as the factual hardware reference for the black FastClix pen, its protective cap and top release plunger. This is a new hand pose; do not copy an earlier image. CRITICAL CAMERA VIEW: look at the PALM SIDE of the patient's index fingertip. Fingerprint ridges and the soft pad must be plainly visible. The fingernail is on the opposite side of the finger, facing AWAY from the camera, completely out of sight. The index finger points vertically upward. The pen approaches horizontally from the RIGHT, its capped end pressing against the RIGHT LATERAL EDGE of the FLESHY fingertip pad, below the nail line and clearly away from the top of the finger. Keep the contact point plainly visible, with skin on every visible side of the cap. Do not place the pen on the fingernail, the nail bed, the very top end of the finger, or the center of the fingerprint pad. Another hand holds the pen naturally with its thumb at the rear release button. Correct anatomy, exactly two adult hands and one real pen. The needle is concealed inside the protective cap. No syringe, exposed needle or blood yet. Neutral gray cotton flight-shirt cuffs, natural skin pores and creases, realistic unpolished plastic, soft cool spacecraft cabin fill. Genuinely transparent alpha background with clean cutout edges. No halo, paper, arrows, text captions, diagram labels, background, vignette or boxes. The purpose is to show the safe side-of-fingertip contact point unmistakably.
prompts.lancingFinal: Edit this photograph to correct ONLY the lancing pen contact location and the holding hand's angle. Keep the real black FastClix device, two natural hands, gray sleeves, photographic lighting and transparent background. The patient's index finger still points upward, PALM/FINGERPRINT side facing the camera. Move the capped end of the pen OFF the right outline/edge of the finger. It must press against the broad SOFT FINGERPRINT PAD ON THE FRONT FACE, at the very distal fingertip, about 4 mm below the rounded top of the finger. The contact point must be on visible soft fingerprint skin, with soft pad skin visibly extending to BOTH the left and right of the capped contact point. The fingernail is on the hidden back of the finger and must not be visible or contacted. Rotate the entire pen and its holding hand toward the camera into a natural diagonal approach so the cap presses into the front of the soft pad, not into the lateral flank. Use a three-quarter camera angle so the viewer can see the real device, the release button under the thumb, AND the clear tip-of-finger soft-pad contact. No exposed needle, no blood, no nail contact, no far-down-the-finger placement. Do not leave the pen touching the outside silhouette of the finger. This is a physical-placement correction, not a style change. Maintain correct natural hand anatomy and a truly transparent background, no text, arrows, highlights or box.
